scope_acknowledged: STT 실패, TTS voice 미사용 가능, 모델 OOM, viseme drift, 모드 감지 실패, 미디어 권한 거부
lens_translation_note: Standard SC3 lens (RFC 7807 problem+json + 4xx/5xx + Retry-After) is reframed for a 100% on-device macOS app. The product still requires an explicit Error Catalog (NSError domain + code + recovery + KO/EN user copy + recoverable-flag), an in-process error envelope (instead of HTTP problem+json), and clearly-defined recovery transitions. 'Retry-After' becomes 'cooldown_ms' or 'backoff_seconds' for STT/TTS/model resume.

findings.issue: There is no Error Catalog artifact named anywhere in the locked design. Without a single canonical catalog (NSError domain + code + recoverable boolean + KO/EN user copy + recovery action), each Swift module will mint its own ad-hoc error type and the failure surface will fragment. SC3 cannot evaluate compliance against an absent object.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: spec-author MUST create `runs/2026-05-05-spec/spec/error-catalog.md` (or `.json`) with at least one row per failure mode listed in this audit. Each row: `{domain, code, severity, recoverable, retry_strategy, user_surface_modality, user_copy_ko, user_copy_en, telemetry_disposition: 'discard'|'local-log-only'|'user-initiated-export'}`. Mirror the function-call signatures pattern used in design-approved.json#function_call_schema_locked_signatures.
findings.evidence: specdd_critic_assignment lists SC3_error_model scope but no upstream artifact provides a catalog skeleton. idea.spec.json no_go bans TODO/mock — implicit errors-as-TODO is therefore disallowed.
findings.spec_action_required: Add `spec/error-catalog.md` to SPEC.md table-of-contents. Define NSError domain prefix (recommend `com.twoweeks.hewassocrates.<subsystem>`).

findings.issue: macOS Speech framework requires TWO independent TCC permissions: (1) NSMicrophoneUsageDescription and (2) NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription. The locked design references neither Info.plist key nor the auth-state machine. SFSpeechRecognizer.requestAuthorization can return `.denied`, `.restricted` (parental controls — directly relevant to M08 child mode), `.notDetermined`, or `.authorized`. App entry without explicit handling will silently fail for any user who declined either prompt.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: SPEC.md MUST define a permission boot sequence: cold-start → check both TCC states → if either is `.denied`/`.restricted`, route to a non-bust 'Permission Required' overlay (text-only, outside character) with a button to System Settings deep-link (`x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Microphone` and `...?Privacy_SpeechRecognition`). Mid-session revocation: AVAudioSession interruption → graceful pause + same overlay.
findings.evidence: Apple Speech framework documentation: SFSpeechRecognizerAuthorizationStatus has 4 cases; both NSMicrophoneUsageDescription (mic) AND NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription (server-eligible recognition) are required for any SFSpeechRecognizer use, even when requiresOnDeviceRecognition=true.
findings.spec_action_required: Add to SPEC.md `Permissions` section: Info.plist usage strings (KO+EN), bootstrap state machine diagram, mid-session revocation flow. Catalog: `STT.PermissionDenied.Microphone`, `STT.PermissionDenied.SpeechRecognition`, `STT.PermissionRestricted.ParentalControl` (latter is COPPA-relevant — must NOT contradict M08).

findings.issue: `requiresOnDeviceRecognition = true` will FAIL with SFSpeechErrorCode.recognizerUnavailable (or similar) when the user's locale model has not been downloaded by macOS. SFSpeechRecognizer.supportsOnDeviceRecognition is a runtime probe — true on-device support is per-locale, per-device, and macOS may not have pre-installed Korean models on a fresh M1/M2 install. A cloud fallback is **forbidden** by idea.spec.json#no_go ('any cloud network call'). The spec has no defined behavior when the on-device locale model is absent.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Cold-start probe: `SFSpeechRecognizer(locale:).supportsOnDeviceRecognition` for ko-KR AND en-US. If either is false, present a one-time guidance overlay: 'macOS System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → System Voice → Manage Voices → Korean (Yuna/Heami) [download required]' AND for STT: 'Settings → General → Language & Region → add Korean → ensure on-device dictation enabled'. Block STT until probe passes. Do NOT silently fall back to server recognition.
findings.evidence: Apple Speech framework: supportsOnDeviceRecognition is documented as locale+device dependent; on-device Korean is gated behind macOS-level model download in System Settings.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `STT Bootstrap` section: probe → block-with-guidance flow. Catalog: `STT.OnDeviceModelMissing.ko_KR`, `STT.OnDeviceModelMissing.en_US`. Recoverable=true after user installs locale.

findings.where: idea.spec.json#ai_capability_required + idea.spec.json#no_go ('any external dependency that requires runtime download from a non-Apple source')
findings.issue: The Gemma E4B Q4 weights file (~3.97GB) MUST be bundled in the .app — but the spec is silent on (a) where in the bundle, (b) integrity verification on first launch, (c) behavior when the bundle's weights file is missing/corrupt (e.g. Gatekeeper quarantine partial extract, antivirus quarantine, user-modified bundle). With no integrity check, the app could load a tampered model and produce invalid function-call JSON in production.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: On first launch and on every cold start, compute SHA-256 of the weights blob and compare against a constant baked into the binary at build time. On mismatch: hard-stop with overlay 'Model integrity check failed. Reinstall from notarized DMG.' (this preserves the no-cloud rule — no automatic re-download). On absence: same hard-stop with `MODEL_BUNDLE_MISSING` code. Document the SHA-256 in spec/model-integrity.md.
findings.evidence: DMG distribution + Apache-2.0 + Mac App Store path means the bundle could exceed the 4GB Mac App Store binary size limit — separate finding (SC3-018) — but integrity is the prerequisite. idea.spec.json#no_go forbids non-Apple runtime download.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Model Bundling` section: bundle path, expected SHA-256, integrity check timing, failure modes. Catalog: `Model.IntegrityMismatch`, `Model.BundleMissing`, `Model.LoadFailed.Corrupt`.

findings.issue: Two install-time guards are missing from the locked design: (a) macOS < 14 (Sonoma), (b) Intel Mac (no Apple Silicon → MLX-Swift will not function). Without LSMinimumSystemVersion + an arch check at first launch, an Intel Mac on macOS 14 will install successfully and crash on first model load with an opaque dyld/CPU error. This is a demo-day catastrophe class — a judge on Intel Mac.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: (a) Set LSMinimumSystemVersion = 14.0 in Info.plist (App Store + DMG installer should refuse). (b) Build as arm64-only (no x86_64 slice). (c) Runtime guard at NSApplicationDidFinishLaunching: detect `sysctlbyname('hw.optional.arm64', ...)`; if 0, present 'This app requires an Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later).' overlay and exit gracefully. (d) Document the M1 8GB caveat (E4B Q4 ~3.97GB + Swift runtime + display compositor = OOM risk on 8GB).
findings.evidence: idea.spec.json claims TTFT ≤12s on M1 — but does not distinguish M1 8GB vs M1 16GB. MLX-Swift requires Apple Silicon; spec-lead must explicitly close this.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `System Requirements & Install-Time Guards` section. Catalog: `OSCompat.IntelMacUnsupported`, `OSCompat.MacOSTooOld`, `OSCompat.M1_8GB_Warning` (severity: warning, not block, but disable thinking-mode pulse to free RAM).

findings.where: design-approved.json#design_tokens (colors define bust state, no error state)
findings.issue: The design system has zero error-surface tokens. The bust must NEVER speak errors (it stays in Socratic character — implicit but not stated). There is no defined modality for surfacing errors (overlay? menu-bar item? but menu bar auto-hides; toast? but fullscreen takeover; settings panel?). With M08 child-mode, error copy must additionally be age-appropriate. Without a defined error-surface modality, each error will be a UX one-off.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Define exactly ONE primary error-surface modality. Recommendation: a centered modal overlay layer ABOVE the bust at z-index higher than thought-silhouette, painterly-frame matching alabaster_bust palette but tinted toward warm_amber_accent for error state, with two action buttons (Try Again / Open Settings / Quit). The bust freezes mid-REST-viseme during overlay. This explicitly separates 'character' (bust) from 'system' (overlay). Add design tokens: `error_overlay_bg`, `error_overlay_border`, `error_text_primary`, `error_text_secondary`, child-mode large-text variant.
findings.evidence: fullscreen_takeover=true + menu_bar_auto_hide=true + bust as sole UI element. No standard macOS chrome is available for errors.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Error Surface Modality` section. Add tokens to design-approved.json `design_tokens.error_*` (or fork → design-approved-v2). Catalog must reference modality per row.

findings.where: idea.spec.json#stack_decisions_locked.tts = 'AVSpeechSynthesizer (system voices: Korean Yuna/Heami, English Samantha/Alex)'
findings.issue: On a fresh macOS 14 install, only one or two compact Korean voices may be present (e.g. Yuna compact). Heami/Yuna 'Premium' or 'Enhanced' voices require manual download via System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → System Voice → Manage Voices. AVSpeechSynthesisVoice(language: 'ko-KR') may return nil or a low-quality compact voice on the judge's demo Mac. The spec does not define the fallback voice ranking or the user-prompt-to-download flow.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Define a voice-resolution algorithm: (1) try Yuna Premium → (2) Yuna Enhanced → (3) Yuna Compact → (4) any ko-KR voice → (5) graceful degrade: 'voice unavailable' overlay with deep-link to Manage Voices. Same for en-US (Samantha → Alex → any). On (5), spec must define: do we proceed with TEXT-ONLY captions and viseme animation driven by phoneme stream from g2p (no audio)? Or block? Recommend: TEXT+viseme degradation with a small dot indicator, since the bust must still 'speak' silently — this preserves the demo even on a janitor-cleaned demo Mac.
findings.evidence: AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.speechVoices() returns only installed voices. Premium voices are >100MB and not pre-installed.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Voice Resolution & Fallback` section. Catalog: `TTS.VoiceUnavailable.ko_KR`, `TTS.VoiceUnavailable.en_US`, `TTS.SynthesizerInitFailed`, `TTS.UtteranceCancelled`.

findings.issue: TTFT budget is specified but no error path defined when budget is exceeded. On a hot-but-thermally-throttled Mac (judge running for 4 hours), TTFT could exceed 30s. The bust would appear frozen mid-thought. Spec defines no inference timeout, no progress signal escalation, no abort path.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Define a soft-timeout (e.g. 15s on M2/M3, 25s on M1) at which the thought-silhouette pulse changes color (oklch variant) or amplitude — surfaces 'still thinking' WITHOUT breaking character. Hard-timeout (e.g. 45s) → cancel inference, return the bust to REST viseme, raise overlay 'The thinking is taking longer than usual. Try a shorter question?'. Also: detect thermal state via ProcessInfo.thermalState (`.serious`/`.critical`) and proactively warn before inference.
findings.evidence: M-series thermal throttling is real; demo-day setup may run hot. No fallback observed in any artifact.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Inference Timeout & Thermal Awareness` section. Catalog: `Model.InferenceTimeout.Soft`, `Model.InferenceTimeout.Hard`, `Model.ThermalThrottle.Warning`.

findings.issue: Gemma function-call output is text-generated JSON — it WILL hallucinate. The locked schema does not specify: (a) JSON-parse failure recovery, (b) wrong function-name returned, (c) required field missing or empty (e.g. ask_back returns `""`), (d) enum value out-of-range (mode_classify returns 'curious_skeptic' instead of one of 4 enums), (e) confidence < threshold (mode_classify says 0.3 — what threshold triggers re-prompt?), (f) all-modes-equal-confidence ambiguity. The bust would speak garbage or freeze. SC2 owns API design but SC3 owns the failure path.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Spec must define for each function: (1) strict JSON schema validation step (use Foundation JSONDecoder + custom validator), (2) on parse failure → 1 retry with stricter prompt, then fallback to a hardcoded safe response per function (e.g. ask_back fallback: '잠시만, 그 질문을 다시 들려줄 수 있나요?' / 'Can you say that one more time?' — preserves character). (3) mode_classify confidence threshold: define explicitly (recommend 0.6 floor, < 0.6 → default to `other` with neutral question template). (4) defer_to_human invocation must always succeed since it's the safety valve — define a hardcoded resource_class fallback.
findings.evidence: Gemma 4 native function-calling is reliable but not perfect. idea.spec.json#no_go forbids TODO/mock — silent-fail on bad function-call output is implicit-mock.
findings.spec_action_required: Cross-reference SC2_api_design (function-call schema is their primary scope) but SC3 owns: per-function fallback responses, confidence thresholds, retry budget. Catalog: `Model.FunctionCall.JSONParseError`, `Model.FunctionCall.UnknownFunctionName`, `Model.FunctionCall.RequiredFieldMissing`, `Model.FunctionCall.EnumOutOfRange`, `Model.FunctionCall.ConfidenceBelowThreshold`.

findings.where: design-approved.json#design_tokens.motion + idea.spec.json#success_criteria ('viseme-audio drift ≤ 50ms RMS') + assets/SOURCE.md (suggests ≤30ms because of beard occlusion)
findings.issue: Drift target is conflicting between artifacts (50ms vs SOURCE.md asks for tighter ≤30ms). No defined behavior when drift exceeds target: snap-resync (jarring), slow-blend (extends drift), abort frame (mouth flicker), pause TTS to let viseme catch up (audio gap). Demo-day risk: drift accumulates over a 30-second utterance and the final word's mouth shape is on the wrong syllable. This is one of the documented demo_day_metrics → high-severity.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Define drift-recovery state machine: (1) measure drift each frame against AVSpeechSynthesizer's willSpeakRangeOfSpeechString delegate timestamp. (2) drift < 33ms (1 frame at 30fps) → no action. (3) 33ms ≤ drift < 100ms → micro-adjust frame duration (skip or repeat one frame). (4) drift ≥ 100ms → snap-resync to current word boundary at next word boundary (NOT mid-word). (5) drift ≥ 250ms (catastrophic, e.g. CPU stall) → freeze on REST viseme, emit Model.VisemeStallRecovery telemetry-local-only. Reduce-Motion mode at 12fps: tolerance scales to 83ms (1 frame).
findings.evidence: design-approved.json#motion has viseme_crossfade_ms=0 (hard cuts), so any drift is highly visible. SOURCE.md beard occlusion observation ratchets up sensitivity.
findings.spec_action_required: Resolve drift-target conflict (recommend ≤33ms RMS = 1-frame tolerance at 30fps). Add SPEC.md `Viseme-Audio Sync State Machine` section. Catalog: `Viseme.DriftMicro`, `Viseme.DriftRecover.SnapToWordBoundary`, `Viseme.StallRecovery`, `Viseme.G2P_Failed.Hangul_Edge_Case`, `Viseme.PhonemeStreamStalled`.

findings.issue: Mixed-language utterance is a stated success criterion but Speech framework requires a single SFSpeechRecognizer instance per locale. Spec is silent on whether the app runs ko-KR and en-US recognizers in parallel and merges, or single-locale 'auto' mode (which doesn't exist in Speech framework as of macOS 14). When the user says 'Why does some 노래 make me 울지?', recognition will likely degrade. There is no defined error/quality path for low-confidence transcription.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Implement a primary-locale + secondary-locale strategy: detect predominant language via SFSpeechRecognitionResult.bestTranscription.segments[].confidence (averaged) on first 1.5s, then commit to one recognizer for the utterance. If both score < 0.5, surface 'I missed that — say it once more?' as a Socratic re-question (preserves character). Define Korean-locale as primary default given target_persona.
findings.evidence: Speech framework SFSpeechRecognizer is locale-bound; no native multilingual mode. The 90% mixed-language target is aspirational without a concrete strategy.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Mixed-Language STT Strategy` section. Catalog: `STT.LowConfidenceTranscription`, `STT.LanguageAmbiguous`, `STT.SilenceTimeout` (silence > 5s = state, not error, recovery: idle bust posture).

findings.issue: SFSpeechRecognizer has TWO undocumented-but-real failure modes that bite production apps: (a) AVAudioSession-style interruption when a system event grabs the mic (FaceTime call notification, Siri trigger, screen sharing start) — recognition task fails mid-utterance with `SFSpeechErrorCode.audioReadFailed` or task cancellation. (b) The 1-minute continuous-recognition limit on some macOS versions/locales silently truncates. The spec defines no recovery for either.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: (a) Subscribe to AVAudioEngine .audioEngineConfigurationChange and .interruption notifications; on interruption, gracefully cancel current SFSpeechRecognitionTask, freeze bust at REST viseme, emit silent overlay 'Listening paused (system interruption). Click to resume.' On resume, restart engine. (b) Auto-rotate recognition tasks every 50s for long-form input (rare in this product but possible if a user reads a long passage).
findings.evidence: Speech framework documentation + community-known macOS limitations.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `STT Lifecycle & Interruption Handling` section. Catalog: `STT.AudioInterruption.SystemEvent`, `STT.RecognitionTaskTimeout`, `STT.AudioReadFailed`.

findings.issue: Core Data / SwiftData failure modes are unspecified: (a) NSPersistentStoreLightweightMigrationOptionKey failure between app versions (schema evolution between W1 and W2 is plausible — `Wonder.thinkingTraceCompressed` field could be added post-W1), (b) disk-full during write (NSError code NSFileWriteOutOfSpaceError), (c) DB file corruption (user copies app from time-machine, partial restore), (d) user manually deletes the .sqlite file mid-session, (e) File Protection complete encryption: when user reboots and unlocks, but app is already running (rare on macOS but possible with FileVault), Core Data writes can fail.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: (a) Define migration policy: lightweight only; a heavyweight migration path triggers an export-to-JSON-and-recreate flow with user confirmation. (b) Pre-flight disk check before each write (≥ 100MB free). (c) Corruption recovery: detect on store load, surface 'Wondering log unreadable. Export attempt? / Start fresh?' overlay. (d) NSPersistentStoreCoordinator monitor for store-removal events. (e) Document that File Protection 'complete' is incompatible with background process — likely should use `completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication` for desktop app.
findings.evidence: regulatory_domain says 'Core Data DB 암호화(File Protection complete)' — this attribute (NSFileProtectionComplete) is iOS-flavored; macOS Core Data uses different APIs and 'complete' may not be the right setting for a long-running desktop app that needs background persistence.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Wondering Log Persistence & Recovery` section. Reconcile File Protection level with macOS desktop semantics. Catalog: `Storage.MigrationFailed`, `Storage.DiskFull`, `Storage.Corruption`, `Storage.StoreUnavailable`, `Storage.EncryptionUnavailable`.

findings.where: idea.spec.json#no_go ('any cloud network call (App Sandbox: no Outgoing)') + design-approved.json#mitigation_adopted_full M04 (OfflineProofBadge)
findings.issue: Spec says '0 byte egress' and M04 promises a visible '0 KB sent' counter, but does not define: (a) HOW the counter is verified (entitlement com.apple.security.network.client = false is necessary but not sufficient — any framework dependency could try to phone home), (b) what happens if MLX-Swift, espeak-ng, or a transitive dep attempts a network call (sandbox will deny → does the app log this and surface? or silently swallow?), (c) crash-reporting framework egress: Apple's CrashReporter sends to Apple by default — does spec disable? (d) Bonjour/local-network egress (e.g. mDNS) — sandbox-allowed by default? Without an audit-test, the OfflineProofBadge is a marketing claim, not an engineering one.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: (a) Set entitlement `com.apple.security.network.client = false` AND `com.apple.security.network.server = false`. (b) At launch, install a NSURLProtocol shim that traps and logs any URL request attempted by any framework — convert to `Sandbox.NetworkAttempt.Blocked` event, increment a counter visible in OfflineProofBadge as 'Blocked: 0'. (c) Disable MetricKit / CrashReporter sharing in Info.plist (`NSAppTransportSecurity.NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=false` is unrelated; the actual key is opting out of MetricKit submission). (d) Document that mDNS is allowed-by-sandbox-default and add explicit test that no UDP/TCP fired except loopback.
findings.evidence: design-approved.json#mitigation_adopted_full M04 is stated as 'video-script.md 0:00-0:30' performance, but engineering verification is absent. video-script.md is a marketing artifact, not a spec.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Network Egress Verification` section + `spec/network-test-plan.md` describing automated test. Catalog: `Sandbox.NetworkAttemptBlocked` (severity: warning, counter increments, but app continues), `Sandbox.EntitlementMisconfigured`.

findings.issue: E4B Q4 weights ≈ 3.97GB. Add Swift runtime, SwiftUI compositor, viseme PNGs, Speech framework working set, AVSpeechSynthesizer, Core Data — total resident set on M1 8GB will likely exceed available memory, triggering jetsam/swap thrashing. Spec has no explicit OOM detection, recovery, or pre-launch RAM check. demo_day_metrics 'TTFT ≤ 12s on M1' is unachievable with severe swap. SPEC must declare M1 8GB as unsupported OR define a degraded mode (fewer viseme PNGs cached, smaller context window, etc).
findings.recovery_path_recommended: (a) Detect physical RAM via `sysctlbyname('hw.memsize', ...)`. If < 16GB, surface a one-time warning at first launch: 'Performance may be reduced on this Mac (8GB RAM detected). Consider M1 16GB+ for best experience.' Continue with launch. (b) Subscribe to memory-pressure notifications (DispatchSource.makeMemoryPressureSource). On `.warning`, free non-essential caches (viseme PNGs evict to disk-backed). On `.critical`, save state and quit gracefully with overlay 'Memory low. Close other apps and reopen.' (c) Define context-window scaling: 256K context is the architectural ceiling, but on memory-pressured devices, dynamically truncate to 64K with user notice.
findings.evidence: MLX-Swift loaded weights are RAM-resident; macOS does not page MLX weight buffers efficiently. M1 8GB total RAM means usable ≈ 5GB after OS — model alone takes 80%.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Memory Management & OOM Recovery` section. Catalog: `Model.MemoryPressure.Warning`, `Model.MemoryPressure.Critical`, `Model.OOMRecovery.GracefulExit`, `Model.RAMInsufficientWarning.M1_8GB`.

findings.where: design-approved.json#mitigation_adopted_full M08 (child-mode COPPA) + this audit's user-surface findings
findings.issue: M08 mandates a child-mode (≤13y) with COPPA flow, 24h retention, and on-device-only data. Error messages MUST be age-appropriate in child mode, but the spec does not differentiate adult vs child error copy. A child seeing 'SFSpeechErrorCode.audioReadFailed' or even 'Microphone permission denied. Open System Settings.' is bad UX and worse for COPPA tone. Also: error messages must NOT collect identifying information from a child during recovery flows (e.g. 'Email this error to support' — forbidden).
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Error catalog (SC3-001) MUST have THREE copy variants per row: `user_copy_ko_adult`, `user_copy_ko_child`, `user_copy_en_adult`, `user_copy_en_child`. Child copy: simpler vocabulary, gentle tone, no jargon, no email collection. Example: adult `STT.PermissionDenied.Microphone` = 'Microphone access is needed. Open Settings to allow it.'; child = '소크라테스가 너의 목소리를 들으려면 도움이 필요해. 어른과 함께 설정을 열어줘.' (Socrates needs help to hear you. Ask a grown-up to open Settings with you.)
findings.evidence: M08 explicitly requires age-appropriate flows; idea.spec.json#user_outcome_metrics references both adult+student personas; M08 mandates COPPA-compliant data flow.
findings.spec_action_required: Update SC3-001 catalog schema to include `user_copy_ko_child`, `user_copy_en_child`, `requires_adult_help: bool`. Add SPEC.md `Child-Mode Error Copy Standards` section.

findings.where: idea.spec.json#user_outcome_metrics ('next-day re-open rate: not measured in MVP (privacy: no telemetry)')
findings.issue: 'No telemetry' is stated, but the spec is silent on crash-reporting policy. macOS by default sends crash reports to Apple via CrashReporter. Apple's MetricKit also auto-sends. With telemetry-free as a stated value, spec must affirmatively define: (a) Apple CrashReporter — opt-out at OS level is user choice (system-wide), but app must NOT enable any additional collection. (b) MetricKit — disable. (c) Local crash dumps — write to `~/Library/Logs/HeWasSocrates/crashdumps/` for user-initiated export (e.g. menu item 'Export diagnostic bundle'). (d) Feature: child mode crash dumps must NOT include user utterances, only stack traces.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Add SPEC.md `Crash & Diagnostic Reporting Policy` section: (a) explicitly disable MetricKit. (b) catch unhandled NSException + Swift fatalError via signal handler, write to local rolling log (10MB cap, oldest-evict). (c) menu-item or settings-panel 'Export diagnostic bundle' that zips logs and reveals in Finder — user-initiated only. (d) child-mode: redact userUtterance fields before write.
findings.evidence: no_go forbids cloud calls; telemetry is stated absent; but absence of explicit policy = default Apple collection occurs.
findings.spec_action_required: Add `Crash & Diagnostic Reporting Policy` to SPEC.md. Catalog: `Diagnostic.LogWriteFailed`, `Diagnostic.LogRotationFailed`. Define menu-item UX for export.

findings.issue: Mac App Store has historical binary size limits (4GB total app bundle on disk, with executable code <500MB). E4B Q4 ≈ 3.97GB weights pushes against this. If MAS rejects, the spec already lists DMG as primary so this is not a hackathon blocker. But the post-hackathon path 'Mac App Store after hackathon' (idea.spec.json line 84) is at risk. Spec should acknowledge.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Add SPEC.md `Distribution Size Constraints` section. Document the bundle size projection. If exceeded, options: (a) reduce to E2B variant (out-of-scope per current spec), (b) split into 'app + sidecar resource bundle' via on-demand resources (App Store-supported, NOT runtime download since it's Apple's CDN — does NOT violate no_go), (c) DMG-only distribution (current primary). Catalog: not needed (build-time check, not runtime).
findings.evidence: Mac App Store size limit ~4GB documented; E4B Q4 = 3.97GB leaves ~30MB for code+assets which is too tight.
findings.spec_action_required: Document the constraint and the 3 options with the recommendation explicit (probably DMG-only for hackathon, ODR for MAS later — Apple-hosted ODR is allowed by no_go because it's an Apple source).

findings.issue: espeak-ng has documented gaps for Korean (especially newly-coined English loanwords transliterated into Hangul, e.g. '컴퓨터'). The fallback is 'AVSpeechSynthesizer phoneme delegate' but that delegate provides English-only IPA in many cases. When g2p produces no phoneme for a syllable, spec defines no fallback viseme — the bust will hold the previous viseme too long, breaking sync.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Define a fallback chain per syllable: (1) espeak-ng → (2) AVSpeechSynthesizer phoneme delegate → (3) syllable-shape heuristic (Hangul jamo → vowel-class mapping → viseme bucket: ㅏ→AA, ㅣ→EE, ㅗ→OH, ㅜ→UH, etc.) → (4) REST + warning increment. Define a `g2p_coverage` metric in success_criteria.
findings.evidence: espeak-ng Korean is community-maintained; not all Hangul edge cases are mapped. design-approved.json#design_tokens.viseme_set lists 16 visemes but the phoneme→viseme map file is referenced but not yet committed (`spec/phoneme-viseme-map.json`).
findings.spec_action_required: Author `spec/phoneme-viseme-map.json` with explicit fallback chain. Catalog: `Viseme.G2P.HangulSyllableUnmapped`, `Viseme.G2P.LoanwordUnknown`.

findings.issue: mode_classify returns confidence:float but spec defines no threshold for action. (a) What if confidence < 0.5 → default to which mode? (b) What if confidence is 0.51 vs 0.49 (boundary thrash on similar utterances within a session)? (c) What if recent_history_compressed conflicts with current utterance (was 'curious_adult', now utterance pattern says 'learning_student')? Mode flapping mid-session degrades demo continuity. Also: defer_to_human is the ONLY safety valve for regulated advice but spec doesn't define WHO calls it: is it always tried first by Gemma's planner, or only after mode_classify returns? Race condition.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: (a) Confidence floor 0.6 → if below, classify as `other` and use neutral question template. (b) Add hysteresis: a session-stable mode requires 2 consecutive same-mode classifications above 0.6. (c) defer_to_human is checked FIRST regardless of mode — it is a safety guard, not a mode. Document the function-call orchestration order: defer_to_human → mode_classify → ask_back / surface_past_wonder.
findings.evidence: confidence:float with no threshold = under-specified. M07 (regulated-advice gate) demands defer_to_human is reliable.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Function-Call Orchestration Order` section + `Mode Classification Hysteresis` rules. Catalog: `Mode.Classify.LowConfidence`, `Mode.Classify.AmbiguousMultiPeak`, `Mode.Flap.HysteresisHold`.

findings.issue: AVSpeechSynthesizer has surprisingly rich failure surface that is unspecified: (a) speakUtterance ignored if synthesizer is mid-utterance and audio session unavailable; (b) speech rate clipping varies by macOS version (AVSpeechUtteranceDefaultSpeechRate is not portable across major OS versions); (c) audio output device disconnect mid-utterance (user unplugs headphones during demo); (d) volume = 0 (muted Mac during demo — bust mouths but no audio). Spec does not define any of these.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: (a) Queue or cancel-and-restart policy: define explicitly. Recommend: cancel-and-restart on user re-utterance (user owns the conversation pace). (b) Use AVSpeechUtteranceDefaultSpeechRate × 1.0 on macOS 14+ explicitly tested; document if drift to macOS 15. (c) Subscribe to AVAudioSession route-change notifications (or AudioObjectPropertyAddress for macOS) → on output device loss, pause speak, surface 'Audio output unavailable. Reconnect speakers/headphones.' overlay. (d) Detect system volume = 0 (or muted) at speak time → small visual indicator '🔇 muted' in caption area, do NOT block (lip-sync still demonstrable visually).
findings.evidence: AVSpeechSynthesizer documented limitations. Demo-day risk: judge's setup may have audio routing issues.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `TTS Lifecycle & Audio Routing` section. Catalog: `TTS.AudioRouteLost`, `TTS.SystemMuted`, `TTS.UtteranceSuperseded`.

findings.issue: Fullscreen takeover means user has no standard macOS escape hatch (Cmd-Q is intercepted in true fullscreen on some macOS versions). When an unrecoverable error occurs, user must be able to exit. Spec does not define keyboard shortcuts for emergency exit, nor does it define what happens if the user presses Esc / Cmd-W / Cmd-Q during error overlay.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Define always-available keyboard contract regardless of state: Esc → exit fullscreen (NSWindow.toggleFullScreen). Cmd-Q → quit app gracefully (cancel inference, close stores, save session). Cmd-W → end session, return to bust REST. Cmd-, → open Settings panel (where permissions/voice management/diagnostic export live). Document in SPEC.md `Keyboard Contract`.
findings.evidence: fullscreen + auto-hide menubar = if error overlay itself crashes, user is stuck.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Keyboard Contract & Emergency Exit` section. Catalog: not needed (defensive UX).

findings.issue: audioFilePathLocal is nullable + 'only if user opt-in'. Edge case: user opts in mid-session, then opts out — what happens to existing audio files? Are they deleted (must be, by privacy default) or orphaned? When user revokes mid-session, current recording: discarded or completed-then-deleted?
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Define cleanup policy: opt-out toggle triggers immediate purge of all audioFilePathLocal-referenced files within 60s, with progress overlay. Mid-recording: stop, do not write final file. Add a SemanticTag scrub also (any tag derived from audio).
findings.evidence: Privacy-by-default principle + GDPR right-to-erasure.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Audio Opt-In Lifecycle` section. Catalog: `Storage.AudioPurgeFailed.PartialCleanup`.

findings.issue: defer_to_human is the only path for regulated topics (legal/medical/financial/emergency). 'emergency' specifically — if a user expresses suicidal ideation or imminent harm, the bust must NOT remain Socratic; it must surface a hard-coded hotline (KO: 1393, EN: 988). Spec mentions 'suggested_resource_class: string' but does not define the resource_class → hotline mapping nor the override of bust character for emergency.
findings.recovery_path_recommended: Add SPEC.md `Emergency Defer Mapping` section: trigger_category='emergency' → bypass bust character, render full-overlay text-only message with locale-correct hotline (KO: 1393 자살예방상담, US-EN: 988). NOT a Socratic question — direct human-help surfacing. This is a low-frequency but high-stakes path; demo video should NOT include this scenario but spec must define.
findings.evidence: M07 = regulated-advice gate. Failure to handle emergency content correctly = ethical and potentially legal liability.
findings.spec_action_required: Add SPEC.md `Emergency Defer Mapping` section. Catalog: `Defer.Emergency.HotlineSurfaced`, `Defer.Emergency.NoLocaleHotline.Fallback`.

scope_coverage_self_assessment: Assigned scope (STT failures, TTS voice unavailable, model OOM, viseme drift, mode-detection failure, media permission denial) is fully covered: STT (SC3-002, 003, 011, 012), TTS (SC3-007, 021), model/OOM (SC3-004, 008, 009, 015), viseme drift (SC3-010, 019), mode detection (SC3-020), media permission (SC3-002 covers both mic + speech recognition + TCC revocation). Beyond strict scope, SC3 expanded into adjacent error-model territory that will be a pre-author gap if not raised now: error catalog absence (SC3-001), error-surface modality (SC3-006), child-mode error copy (SC3-016), os-compat install guards (SC3-005), bundle integrity (SC3-004), wondering-log persistence (SC3-013), sandbox egress verification (SC3-014), crash policy (SC3-017), audio opt-in lifecycle (SC3-023), emergency defer (SC3-024), and keyboard escape contract (SC3-022). One topic adjacent to SC3 but explicitly owned by SC2 (function-call schema design) is referenced (SC3-009) only at the failure-path level.
